newsitem.title: USA: JonBenet inquiry in Colorado said to be nearing end.
newsitem.headline: JonBenet inquiry in Colorado said to be nearing end.

text.p: Police have nearly finished investigating JonBenet Ramsey's slaying and could present their findings to the district attorney by late August or early September, the Rocky Mountain News reported Friday.
Authorities in Boulder, Colorado were not available to comment on the report.
No one has been arrested and no suspects have been named in the seven-month-long murder investigation of the six-year-old beauty pageant winner.

When the findings are presented to Boulder County DA Alex Hunter, he could charge someone, turn the matter over to a grand jury, seek more information or reject the case as unsuitable for prosecution.
John Ramsey, father of the young victim, plans to take out advertisements in local newspapers on Sunday to publicise a possible profile of the killer developed by his own team of experts.
He has expressed disappointment that police have focused on the Ramsey family in their investigation, according to a statement he issued earlier this week.

The child's body was found Dec. 26 in the basement of the family's home in Boulder by her father hours after her mother, Patricia, said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000. The parents have denied all involvement in the murder.
The family has moved to Atlanta where they lived before moving to Colorado in the early 1990s. John Ramsey commutes to Colorado where he heads Access Graphics, a computer company.
